Layout.title: Ronny Cajas — Self-custody Bitcoin mentorship
Layout.description: I teach individuals and companies to hold their own Bitcoin, in wallets they control.

AcademyPage.metadataDescription: A wallet architecture knowledge base and the expert track.
AcademyPage.title: To stay safe, you need hard knowledge.
AcademyPage.subtitle: Bitcoin Self-custody is a technical skill. No need to be an expert, but you need to understand the fundamentals.

fundamentals.title: Fundamentals
fundamentals.description: Begin with Bitcoin itself: the network, its money, and how it reaches agreement.

advanced.title: Advanced topics
advanced.description: Go deeper into wallet design, stronger security models, and guided practice.

bitcoinBasics.title: What is Bitcoin?
bitcoinBasics.description: Explore Bitcoin as a peer-to-peer monetary network and the problem it was designed to solve.

transactions.title: Transactions and UTXOs
transactions.description: Learn how value moves across the network and how unspent transaction outputs work.

blockchain.title: Blocks and the blockchain
blockchain.description: See how transactions are grouped into blocks and linked into a shared ledger.

consensus.title: Mining and consensus
consensus.description: Understand proof of work and how independent nodes agree on Bitcoin's history.

architectures.title: Wallet architectures
architectures.description: Explore how popular wallets are built, where their keys live, and how they have failed.

threatModels.title: Threat modeling
threatModels.description: Identify what you need to protect and choose safeguards that fit your situation.

multisig.title: Multisignature and distributed security
multisig.description: Understand how multiple keys can share control and reduce single points of failure.

mentorship.title: Guided setup and review
mentorship.description: Work one-to-one to design, build, and verify a personal self-custody setup.

HomePage.metadataDescription: Learn to hold your own Bitcoin in a wallet you control — without custodians, and without trusting an app, a device, or unaudited code with your keys.

hero.title: Own your Bitcoin, not a wallet you don't really control.
hero.subtitle: Wallets like Trezor and Coldcard leave your private keys exposed. Learn how to create and manage wallets that are truly secure

HomePage.metricLabel: dollars in Bitcoin our clients now hold in self-custody — under keys only they control.

learningSection.title: Why these wallets fail, and why they will keep failing?
learningSection.body: Your Bitcoin is safe when you have the right knowledge, not when you buy a device. Bitcoin already has the tools, you just need to learn how to use them.

offering.title: Plans
offering.subtitle: One-off sessions, a subscription, or ongoing consultancy.

PremiumPage.metadataTitle: Become an expert — 1:1 Bitcoin self-custody mentorship
PremiumPage.metadataDescription: One-to-one sessions to design, build and verify your own Bitcoin self-custody setup, at a convenient price.
PremiumPage.title: Be an expert for a convenient price
PremiumPage.subtitle: The knowledge is free; the difference is having someone who sits with you, reviews your hardware and walks you through your first transaction — until you can verify it yourself.

setup.title: Designing your setup
setup.body: Which hardware, how many keys, one device or a multisig — chosen against your threat model, not a sales page.

keys.title: Generating and storing keys
keys.body: Dice, entropy, backups, passphrases and metal. We do it once, together, and you write it down in a way you can actually recover.

verify.title: Verifying instead of trusting
verify.body: You build and sign a real transaction, then check it with your own node and your own eyes.

support.title: Keep asking
support.body: A subscription keeps the conversation open while your setup, the firmware or the threats change.

PremiumPage.architecturesTitle: Want to explore on your own?
PremiumPage.architecturesBody: Browse the architecture of popular wallets, where their keys live, and their documented failures.

FirmwareDiagram.model: threat model — what malicious firmware could reach
FirmwareDiagram.prompt: Select any element to see its full name and what malicious firmware could do with it.
FirmwareDiagram.caption: Simplified threat model of the Trezor Safe 5: if the signed firmware image itself were malicious, these are the parts of the device it could lie about or abuse. The secure element is shown because firmware might try to attack it — not because it is easy to infect.

display.name: Touchscreen display
display.description: Shows an address, amount or fee that differs from the transaction it actually signs.

touch.name: Touch confirmation
touch.description: Registers a tap you never made, so a payout looks approved on the spot.

usb.name: USB data link
usb.description: Tells Trezor Suite the balance and recipient it expects while sending something else to the chip.

seed.name: Seed and private keys
seed.description: Reads the decrypted seed from device memory and signs transactions of its own.

passphrase.name: Passphrase entry
passphrase.description: Captures the passphrase as it is typed and clones every hidden wallet it unlocks.

storage.name: Firmware storage
storage.description: Rewrites its own image and re-infects the device after a factory reset.

secure-element.name: Secure element
secure-element.description: Replays PIN attempts past the limit and hides the counters that would expose it.

randomness.name: Random number generator
randomness.description: Feeds rigged entropy, so keys generated after infection can be guessed.

WalletKnowledge.metadataTitle: Wallet architectures — how popular wallets are built
WalletKnowledge.metadataDescription: A knowledge base of Bitcoin wallet architectures: how each brand is built, where its keys live, and how it has failed in public.
WalletKnowledge.title: Wallet architectures
WalletKnowledge.subtitle: Pick a wallet to see how it is built, where its keys live, and every failure documented so far.

riskScale.title: How exposed are your funds, really?
riskScale.subtitle: Scale of risk

custodial.label: Critical
custodial.title: Custodial wallets and exchanges
custodial.body: Your keys live on a server you do not control. The platform can freeze, lose, or leak your funds — and if it fails, you are a creditor, not an owner.

hot.label: High
hot.title: Hot software wallets
hot.body: The keys sit on an online device, next to the apps you install and the links you open. Malware or a convincing page can read them before you notice.

commercial-cold.label: Caution
commercial-cold.title: Commercial cold wallets
commercial-cold.body: The keys stay offline, but the wallet runs firmware you cannot inspect, on hardware heavily exposed to supply chain risks.
commercial-cold.examples: Ledger, Trezor, Tangem, COLDCARD, and similar hardware wallets.

opensource-verifiable.label: Safe
opensource-verifiable.title: Verifiable open-source self-custody
opensource-verifiable.body: You learn to identify misleading wallet setups. You create your own secure wallet using open-source tools.
